auth.notes: Tuya account + cloud-issued pairing; device-side auth for the BLE session is the device uuid / local key pair issued at pairing.

endpoints.name: Tuya OpenAPI / app API
endpoints.notes: No tuya*.com hostnames appear as plaintext anywhere in the Smart Life app — region endpoints are delivered at runtime by Tuya's config service. The hosts listed are the publicly documented Tuya endpoint families, recorded for orientation.

cloud.failure_mode: Stock firmware is dead without Tuya cloud at PAIRING time: pairing needs a Tuya account (the local key is cloud-issued), and the encrypted session cannot be established without it. Once paired and the device id + local key are extracted, day-to-day local monitoring (ha_tuya_ble / python-tuya-ble over direct BLE) keeps working with the Tuya cloud gone — the sensor never touches Wi-Fi itself. Remote access, Alexa/Google and cloud automations die with the cloud or the optional BLE gateway. SGS01BTHome removes the cloud dependency for SGS01; SGS01B has only the V1.1Pre2 development image, not a production-ready replacement path.
cloud.notes: The ONLY hard cloud dependency for local use is one-time pairing + key extraction: pair in Smart Life, link the account to a free Tuya IoT developer project, pull device id + local key (tuya-iot-py-sdk / ha_tuya_ble automate this). Tuya has broken this flow for some account types in the past — verify current status before buying hardware for a local-only install. The device UI in the vendor app is a cloud-delivered RN panel: zero hits for `zwjcy` anywhere in the Smart Life app; only the generic BLE transport machinery is in it.
cloud.vendor_service: Tuya cloud (Smart Life / Tuya Smart platform)

discovery.none: Manual selection is required until the generic BLE schema/mobile matcher supports service data. Protocol-4 advertisements use FD50 service data; classic protocol <=3 falls back to A201, both with company 0x07D0. Neither is an advertised GATT service UUID or product-specific identity, and putting either in an invisible discovery.service_data key would make the spec look matched when no consumer can match it. Confirm the product ID and protocol-specific GATT layout before starting a session.
discovery.notes: Advertisements are connectable and carry identity, never sensor values. Confidence: reported (community integrations + the Smart Life BLE SDK), not captured by this project.

identification.notes: No manufacturer, service or local-name matcher is declared: generic Tuya advertisements must not auto-select this spec. Distinguishing a soil tester from any other Tuya BLE single-point device requires manual selection and product-ID confirmation from the vendor binding or a device-info/DP exchange. Service-data 0xFD50 and 0xA201 plus company 0x07D0 are documentary platform evidence only, retained under protocol_details.tuya_ble_protocol.advertising, not an advertised GATT service UUID. The post-connection GATT services have their own protocol-specific mappings below.

device.manufacturer: Tuya (platform) / Shenzhen HaiHao Electronic Co., LTD (canonical SGS01) + white-label clones
device.name: Tuya Bluetooth Soil Tester (zwjcy / SGS01 family)
device.notes:
A battery-powered (2×AAA) probe that measures soil moisture and temperature, marketed as "works with Alexa & Google". Internally it is a two-processor device (per the haraldapp/SGS01BTHome teardown): a Tuya BT3L module on SGS01 or BTU module on SGS01B (both Telink TLSR8250, 512 KB flash) runs stock Tuya BLE firmware and owns the radio, while a separate third-party MCU owns the actual measurement, button and LED. The two are linked by UART running the standard Tuya MCU serial protocol (the same frame family as TuyaMCU Wi-Fi devices); SGS01B uses a different baud rate handled by the replacement firmware's auto-detection.
PROTOCOL: this is a Tuya BLE "single-point" device — connectable GATT, NOT BLE mesh and NOT a passive beacon. Advertisements carry device identity only, never sensor readings; the ble_monitor project confirms SGS01 cannot be supported passively. Selection is manual because the generic matcher has no service_data key: classic <=3 advertisements use A201 and protocol-4 advertisements use FD50 service data, both with company ID 0x07D0. Protocol <=3 uses GATT service 0x1910 with write 0x2B11 and notify 0x2B10. Protocol 4 instead uses service 0xFD50 with write 00000001-0000-1001-8001-00805f9b07d0 and notify 00000002-0000-1001-8001-00805f9b07d0; those characteristics are not part of service 0x1910 and must never be mixed with it. All state moves as encrypted Tuya DP (datapoint) frames on the protocol-specific endpoints. The BLE v3 secret is the first six local-key characters: login_key = MD5(secret), and session_key = MD5(secret || six-byte device_random). PAIR still carries the UUID, but UUID is not a session-key input. These v3 derivations are not generalized to protocol 4. A local integration needs the device id + local key from a Tuya IoT cloud account — the same one-time key-extraction step as Tuya Wi-Fi devices.
HUB QUESTION: with the phone nearby, Smart Life talks to the device directly over BLE — no hub needed for in-range monitoring. Remote access, Alexa/Google and cloud automations require a Tuya Bluetooth gateway (or multi-mode ZigBee+BLE gateway) bridging the BLE sub-device to Wi-Fi/cloud; the "works with Alexa" marketing presupposes that gateway. The device cannot be cloud-controlled standalone.
CLOUD-FREE PATH: SGS01 uses BT3L and SGS01B uses BTU; both contain a Telink TLSR8250 with SWS flashing pads (chip type B85). haraldapp/ SGS01BTHome turns them into BTHome v2 (optionally encrypted) passive advertisers with a GATT config profile and OTA — no Tuya account, keys or encryption session. The stable image covers SGS01. SGS01B (product gpkyrocn) is covered only by the V1.1Pre2 development image, which is not production-ready; it needs BTU-specific activation/unlock and an extra soldered wire for battery-voltage reporting.

openness.notes: Tuya publishes nothing about this category. The transport facts here are corroborated by two independent implementations (python-tuya-ble and the Tuya BLE SDK inside the Smart Life app); the DP maps come from the ha_tuya_ble integration and HA's cloud schema dumps and are marked `reported`, not byte-verified against hardware.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: A factory-fresh or freshly reset tester advertises in pairing mode on its own; the procedure below is for a device that is already bound.

procedures.basis: The vendor quick-start guide for this class of Tuya BLE device. Not replayed against hardware; the exact control differs across the models this spec covers.
procedures.name: Insert batteries, or hold the reset pin, until it advertises in pairing mode

steps.action: Insert the batteries, or hold the reset pin on an already-bound tester.
steps.expect: The tester advertises A201 (classic <=3) or FD50 (protocol 4) service data plus manufacturer company ID 0x07D0 in pairing mode; manually select the product and confirm the protocol-specific GATT service.

exclusivity.notes: One binding: a tester belongs to exactly one Tuya account at a time (others reach it through that account's home sharing), and the local key is that binding's. One connection at a time is the normal behaviour of the stock single-link Tuya BLE firmware rather than something a source states for this model.
exclusivity.recovery: Force-close Smart Life / Tuya Smart on every phone near the tester, and power down any Tuya Bluetooth gateway that has it, before connecting. A tester bound to someone else's account cannot be added to yours until they remove it or it is reset — and either way the local key changes.

pairing.notes: Nothing is readable at all without completing this: BLE v3 derives its session key from the local-key secret and six-byte device_random, both obtained only through the paired session, so a stock Tuya BLE device is inert to an unpaired client. UUID is carried by PAIR but is not a KDF input. The one hard cloud dependency is one-time — once the device id and local key are extracted, day-to-day local monitoring keeps working with the Tuya cloud gone entirely.

pin.notes: Not a PIN: a device id and 16-character local key, issued by Tuya's cloud during the vendor-app pairing and recoverable afterwards through a Tuya IoT developer project. Per-unit, and rotated whenever the device is unbound and paired again.

unpair.clears: The Tuya account binding and the pairing keys; the device returns to advertising in pairing mode and is issued a new device id and local key on the next pairing.
unpair.notes: Unbinding and factory reset are the same operation on this device, and it is destructive to local access in a way users do not expect: any client holding the old local key stops working, and the replacement key can only be obtained by pairing through the vendor app and cloud again. Moving the tester to a different Tuya account means exactly this — unbind, re-pair, re-extract.

issued_to_client: device id + 16-char local key (recoverable via Tuya IoT developer account + tuya-iot-py-sdk)
credentials.notes: The local key IS the credential for the encrypted BLE session — treat it as a password.
stored_on_device: Tuya UUID and device ID (pairing identity)
Six-character local-key-derived secret and per-session keys derived with the six-byte device_random

factory_reset.effect: Unbinds the device from its Tuya account and clears the pairing keys; on re-pairing a new device id / local key pair is issued. The measurement MCU and its calibration are unaffected.

steps.action: Remove the device in the Smart Life / Tuya Smart app (device settings → remove device).
steps.notes: The app drives an UNBIND (function code 0x0005) or DEVICE_RESET (0x0006) frame over GATT; the device returns to advertising in pairing mode. A physical button-hold reset likely exists on the probe's single button (generic Tuya BLE behavior) but is NOT documented for this family — unverified.

steps.action: Flash the exact SGS01 or SGS01B image over the Tuya module's SWS pads (Telink BDT or pvvx TlsrComSwireWriter).
steps.notes: Replaces the whole Tuya stack; afterwards there is no Tuya state to reset. Flash above 0x70000 holds factory MAC/calibration — preserve it. SGS01 uses BT3L and the stable image. SGS01B uses BTU/TLSR8250 and only the V1.1Pre2 development image, which is not production-ready; follow its BTU activation/unlock and battery-measurement precautions.

methods.description: A stock Tuya BLE device yields nothing until it has been paired. The route has two phases — pair once in Smart Life or Tuya Smart to issue the device ID and local key, then connect directly and derive the BLE v3 login/session keys from the six-character secret and the session's six-byte device_random, with no hub and no cloud at runtime.
methods.name: Pair once in the vendor app, then run the session yourself

stages.description: Standard Tuya BLE pairing in the vendor app after manual product selection: classic protocol <=3 advertisements use A201 service data and protocol-4 advertisements use FD50 service data, both with company ID 0x07D0. These service-data records are not the advertised GATT service UUIDs. The app selects service 0x1910 with 0x2B11/0x2B10 for protocol <=3, or service 0xFD50 with the two 128-bit Tuya characteristics for protocol 4, then exchanges PAIR frames (function code 0x0001) carrying the cloud-issued credentials. Requires a Tuya cloud account in Smart Life or Tuya Smart. No protocol-3 session or KDF claim is generalized to protocol 4.
stages.name: Pair in the vendor app, and extract the keys

steps.action: Put the tester in pairing mode (per the vendor quick-start: batteries in / reset pin held), then manually select the product rather than relying on an unsupported service_data matcher. Expect A201 for classic <=3 or FD50 for protocol 4, plus manufacturer company ID 0x07D0.
Confirm product ID and protocol version, then connect to service 0x1910 for protocol <=3 or 0xFD50 for protocol 4; use only the write and notify characteristics assigned to that version below.
Exchange PAIR frames (function code 0x0001) carrying the cloud-issued credentials, binding the device to the account.
steps.expect: The device appears in Smart Life / Tuya Smart and its uuid and local_key exist in the account.

stages.description: After one-time key extraction (device id + local key via a Tuya IoT developer account), a third-party client connects directly and runs the encrypted session itself — the python-tuya-ble / ha_tuya_ble path. No hub, no cloud at runtime.
stages.name: Run the encrypted session from a third-party client

steps.action: Pair the device once through the vendor app (the ble_provisioning method above); local access needs the credentials that pairing creates.
Fetch the device `uuid` and 16-char `local_key` once from a Tuya IoT developer account (the ha_tuya_ble / tuya-iot-py-sdk flow).
steps.expect: Both secrets in hand; no cloud contact is needed after this.

steps.action: Connect directly and run the encrypted DP session with those keys — no hub and no cloud at runtime.

setup.notes: Unlike a plain BLE sensor, a stock Tuya BLE device must be PAIRED before it yields anything. PAIR carries the UUID, six-character secret and device ID; the secret comes from the cloud-issued local_key. BLE v3 then uses login_key = MD5(secret) and session_key = MD5(secret || six-byte device_random), not the UUID, for subsequent encrypted DP traffic. For third-party local access the device id and local key are fetched once from a Tuya IoT developer account (the ha_tuya_ble / tuya-iot-py-sdk flow). Not replayed against this hardware by this project.

rejoin.notes: BLE device — there is no network credential to rotate. Re-binding to a new Tuya account means unbind + re-pair.

testing.notes: No hardware has been exercised by this project. Every fact below is derived from community clean-room work (PlusPlus-ua/python-tuya-ble, garnser/ha_tuya_ble, haraldapp/SGS01BTHome, Home Assistant's Tuya integration) cross-checked against clean-room static analysis of the Smart Life app (see `evidence`), whose BLE SDK carries the transport constants and function codes used here. The DP tables are integration-derived and NOT byte-verified against a live device; the Tuya category `zwjcy` has no official public DP schema at all.

variants.notes: Canonical unit (Shenzhen HaiHao Electronic). Tuya category `zwjcy`; current product id. DP map in `dps.table` below. Supported by ha_tuya_ble and by the SGS01BTHome replacement firmware.

Same form factor and DPs, certified under Tuya category `wsdcg` (temperature/humidity sensor) with different DP numbering — see `dps.wsdcg_variants`.

variants.model: wsdcg-category BLE soil tester (alt DP numbering)

enter.notes: The reported protocol-3 stock update runs inside the encrypted session as function codes 0x000C..0x0010 through `ota_transfer` on 0x2B11 within service 0x1910. Protocol 4 instead uses service 0000fd50-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and write 00000001-0000-1001-8001-00805f9b07d0, but its exact OTA exchange is not established and no command is declared. Whether either module receives the image in place or reboots first is not recorded.

local_access.notes: The Tuya BLE GATT protocol is native local access once the device id + local key are known — direct BLE, no bridge hardware, using the endpoint set for the reported protocol version. The catalogue integration is identify_only because the stock session needs a dedicated stateful encrypted handler; description-only commands are not generic fixed writes. Home Assistant path: garnser/ha_tuya_ble (HACS), which ships DP maps for gvygg3m8 and the wsdcg variants and uses tuya-iot-py-sdk for key retrieval. SGS01BTHome removes keys and cloud on SGS01. SGS01B is BTU/TLSR8250 product gpkyrocn and has only the V1.1Pre2 development image; its support and DP/session behavior remain reported, not production-ready or project-verified.

table.description: Temperature; raw value is tenths of a degree (divide by 10).
°C/°F unit preference. Seen in the cloud schema but not mapped to a BLE DP id in any community source — likely cloud-level only on this product. Unverified.

wsdcg_variants.notes: Same form factor and readings under Tuya category `wsdcg` (temperature/humidity), different DP numbering:

table.notes: Temperature raw value ÷10, same as the zwjcy map.
No battery DPs documented for this variant.

advertising.notes: Reported identity only; no sensor readings are ever broadcast.

protocol_4.role: Protocol-4 identity record; the maintained implementation tries FD50 before the classic fallback

advertising.selection: Manual product-ID and protocol/GATT confirmation is required because the generic BLE schema/mobile matcher has no service_data key; neither service-data UUID is an advertised GATT service UUID or soil-specific identity.

authentication.login_key: MD5(secret), as the 16 raw digest bytes.
authentication.pair: PAIR (function 0x0001) carries the UUID, secret and device ID padded to 44 bytes. UUID remains pairing data, not an input to either MD5 derivation above.
authentication.scope: Maintained-client Tuya BLE v3 behavior; do not generalize this derivation to DP_V4.
authentication.secret: ASCII bytes of the first six characters of the cloud-issued 16-character local_key.
authentication.session_key: MD5(secret || device_random), where device_random is exactly six bytes from the session negotiation; the UUID is NOT a session-key input.

synthetic_vector.notes: Dummy documentation values only, not credentials or a captured session.

dp_types.record_layout: [dp id u8][type u8][length u8][payload, exactly length bytes]
dp_types.scope: Tuya BLE v3 DP records; DP_V4 is not covered by this length rule.
dp_types.signedness: Decode VALUE and ENUM as signed big-endian integers of the declared length. Encode VALUE writes as signed four-byte big-endian.
dp_types.types: RAW=0x00, BOOL=0x01, VALUE=0x02, STRING=0x03, ENUM=0x04, BITMAP=0x05.
dp_types.vector_decode: DP5 VALUE length 4 = -10 -> -1.0 C after scale 0.1; DP3 VALUE length 4 = 50 -> 50 % moisture. A two-byte-length parser desynchronizes immediately.

gatt.selection: Choose one complete endpoint set from the reported protocol version; never combine service 0xFD50 with 0x2B11/0x2B10.

tuya_ble_protocol.transport: BLE GATT, encrypted session, default ATT MTU 20

tuyamcu_uart.link: UART between BT3L on SGS01 or BTU on SGS01B and the sensor MCU; replacement firmware auto-detects their different baud rates
tuyamcu_uart.role: The sensor MCU owns measurement, button and LED; the Tuya module reports its state as DPs. Factory MAC/calibration live above 0x70000 — preserve when reflashing. This hardware fact does not establish the stock BLE protocol generation or validate the SGS01B development image.

remaining_unknowns:
The complete byte-level AES packet framing of the protocol-specific writes remains outside the generic command templates: per-frame sequence numbers, nonce state and chunking depend on the paired session. The BLE v3 secret, login/session MD5 derivations and PAIR boundary are explicit in protocol_details, but the schema has no executable stateful encryption declaration; protocol-4 writes deliberately have no command templates.
DP_V4 is not covered by the BLE v3 one-byte DP length or the KDF above. Establish its length width, random-value location and session behavior from a captured, decrypted SGS01 DP_V4 exchange before generalizing.
Each physical model's actual protocol/GATT generation needs a device-info and service dump. In particular SGS01B (BTU/TLSR8250, gpkyrocn) has only a community-reported DP map and a V1.1Pre2 development replacement image; neither its stock protocol-3/4 generation nor production readiness is asserted.

device_info.description: Query device info (function code 0x0000): device id, product id, firmware and protocol version.

dp_query.description: Request current protocol-3 DP values (function code 0x0002). Reports arrive on 0x2B10 as 0x8001; DPS_V4 is not this command.

ota_transfer.advanced_reason: Writes new firmware to the BT3L/BTU radio module. An image for the wrong module or an interrupted transfer can leave the sensor without a working radio; wired recovery uses the SWS pads while keeping factory data above 0x70000.
ota_transfer.description: Reported protocol-3 firmware update block transfer (function codes 0x000C..0x0010). Exact image behavior is not established; do not generalize this command to the protocol-4 write endpoint.

pair.description: Pairing handshake (function code 0x0001): carries UUID, secret and device ID padded to 44 bytes. The six-character local-key secret gives login_key = MD5(secret); the later session key is MD5(secret || six-byte device_random). UUID is not a KDF input. Not expressible as fixed bytes because the exchange carries per-session random state.

unbind.description: Unbind from the Tuya account (function code 0x0005).

characteristics.name: Protocol <=3 write
characteristics.notes: All host→device v3 commands: pairing, DP query/set, device info, unbind/reset and the reported OTA functions. Byte format is the Tuya BLE encrypted packet, chunked at the 20-byte default MTU; the full stateful framing remains in python-tuya-ble.

characteristics.name: Protocol <=3 notify
characteristics.notes: Protocol-3 DP reports (0x8001) carrying the sensor DPs, time requests (0x8011/0x8012) and command responses. Subscribe before the session exchange; sensor readings never arrive in advertisements. V4 report 0x8006 belongs to protocol 4, not this characteristic's protocol-3 profile.

services.name: Tuya BLE protocol <=3 service
services.notes: Protocol <=3 carries encrypted framed commands on 0x2B11 and responses/reports on 0x2B10 within this 0x1910 service. Default ATT MTU 20; frames are chunked/reassembled by the protocol layer. BLE v3 session_key = MD5(local-key secret || six-byte device_random); UUID is not a session-key input. Do not substitute the protocol-4 service or its 128-bit characteristics.

characteristics.name: Protocol-4 write
characteristics.notes: Protocol-4 host writes, including separately reported DPS_V4 0x0027 after an appropriate protocol-4 session has been established. Do not move this characteristic to service 0x1910 or treat it as 0x2B11. Exact protocol-4 session and OTA behavior remain open.

characteristics.name: Protocol-4 notify
characteristics.notes: Protocol-4 responses and DP_V4 reports (0x8006). Subscribe before protocol-4 negotiation; do not decode these payloads with the v3 one-byte-length rule without independent evidence.

services.name: Tuya BLE protocol-4 service
services.notes: Protocol 4 uses a different service and two Tuya-specific 128-bit characteristics below. Its reported advertisement uses FD50 service data, not A201 and not an assumed advertised GATT service UUID; manual product selection is still required. This entry does not claim that the v3 KDF, one-byte DP record length, OTA command or session implementation works unchanged on protocol 4; no fixed commands are declared here.
